correctness.rationale: For all irreducible two-dimensional Metzler generators the Cayley–Hamilton exponential is exact and yields the factorized trace difference. The determinant is constant in phase; strictly positive monodromy has two positive real eigenvalues and its Perron root is strictly increasing in trace. The hyperbolic identity gives the unique maximum and exact arcosh window; the determinant(I-Q) sign is valid since the minor positive eigenvalue remains below one when synchronized Q is stable. Common-crowding integrating factor yields an exact Poincare map; Perron decomposition gives global extinction, unique positive periodic population, and critical 1/n law. The rational witness was independently calculated entrywise and verified in standalone code with no tolerance in sign inequalities. Limits include constant generator and shared crowding only.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2025 Culex work examines spatial dispersal and sprayed controls but provides numerical weather-dependent scenarios rather than an all-parameter two-pulse timing theorem. The strongest inspected two-patch culling papers (Terry 2010 and Georgescu et al. 2010) establish simultaneous-culling sufficiency or Floquet stability under different mixed controls; neither materially inspected theorem states the exact trace-excess law for varying one patch-specific pulse phase. Gao et al. prove a homogeneous SIS synchrony advantage; the qualitative effect is not new, but its scalar model cannot yield the asymmetric two-by-two hyperbolic phase formula and exact reverse-extinction example by specialization. The 2026 general impulsive permanence theorem does not express a sharp phase-dependent principal eigenvalue. Research-record search and accessible previous work yielded no covering claim. Residual risk from inaccessible Xie et al. (2014) and general positive matrix-product literature remains; absence of hits alone is not proof of originality.

value.rationale: Recent Culex spraying research explicitly studies patch dispersal and spatially/temporally coordinated spraying, making the effect of a fixed relative scheduling offset a natural ecological question. Unlike a routine local stability computation, the finding gives a parameter-uniform strict scheduling optimum under arbitrary patch heterogeneity, an exact necessary-and-sufficient open persistence window, and a complete rational example where an otherwise identical intervention schedule flips global extinction to stable periodic persistence. The exact interval can be used to distinguish the efficacy of independently scheduled regional control campaigns in simplified models. It does not claim a new generic synchrony principle already found by Gao et al., nor epidemiological field predictions.
